title: Though Wandering in a Stranger-land
description: Though Wandering in a Stranger-land in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 88, “The Great Temple”, where the book credits them to Fox's Hymns.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Though wan-dering in a stran-ger land, Though on the waste no al-tar stand, Take com-fort! thou art not a-lone, While Faith hath marked thee for her own.

lines: Though on the waste no altar stand,
Take comfort! thou art not alone,
While Faith hath marked thee for her own.
Wouldst thou a temple? look above, —
The heavens stretch over all in love;
A book? for thine evangel scan
And though no organ-peal be heard,
In harmony the winds are stirred;
And there the morning stars upraise
Their ancient songs of deathless praise.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
